intended_object: The PBW (normal-ordered monomial) basis of the n-th Weyl algebra A_n(k): its basis vectors are the ordered monomials x^α ∂^β, indexed by exponent vectors m : (Fin n ⊕ Fin n) →₀ ℕ. I took this from the docstring, the name, and the lemma `presentedNormalFormBasis_eq_orderedMonomial` just after it.
explanation:
The definition takes Mathlib's standard monomial basis `MvPolynomial.basisMonomials` of the commutative polynomial ring k[x₁..xₙ, ξ₁..ξₙ]. It transports that basis along the inverse of the library's normal-form linear equivalence `presentedNormalFormLinearEquiv : PresentedWeyl k n ≃ₗ[k] SymbolRing k n`.

This equivalence sends generators to variables (`presentedNormalFormLinearEquiv_generator`). It also sends each ordered monomial to the corresponding commutative monomial (`presentedOrderedMonomial_normal`). The library then proves that the basis vector at m is exactly the ordered monomial ∏ xᵢ^{m(inl i)} ∂ᵢ^{m(inr i)} (`presentedNormalFormBasis_eq_orderedMonomial`). So the definition is the standard PBW basis of the Weyl algebra, with the expected indexing.

The restriction to a field is not something this definition adds. It comes from the library's construction of `PresentedWeyl`, which is set up over a field for the Stafford project. The definition only transports a basis along an equivalence the library already has. Mathlib has neither a Weyl algebra nor its PBW basis, so there is no more general counterpart to cite.
